method: Read page by page from the scanned source PDF (88 pages, no text layer, no OCR — every figure read visually), then cross-checked row by row against an independent prior digitisation. 1,392 of 1,392 rows agreed. Two real errors in the prior digitisation were found and corrected: 7A2001 (16.82 -> 76.82) and 11A2002/11A3002 (daughter anchorage 0 -> 0.13).

source_defects.schedule: First Schedule: Port Dues
source_defects.note: The section header row for Containers is printed '1B10001' where it should be the section code 1B10000 — the same number as its first data row.

source_defects.schedule: First Schedule: Port Dues
source_defects.note: The ISPS section header is printed 'L. ISPS DUES' but its codes are 1J…, and the section that follows Fire Safety alphabetically is J. The letter L is a typo in the tariff; recorded as J.

source_defects.schedule: First Schedule: Port Dues
source_defects.note: The PIDD section header is printed 'M. PORT INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT DUES (PIDD)' but its codes are 1K…. The letter M is a typo in the tariff; recorded as K. This is the second such letter slip in the First Schedule (see page 4, ISPS printed as 'L').

source_defects.schedule: Third Schedule: Stevedoring Charges
source_defects.note: 3D2000 skips two sequence numbers in the PUBLISHED table: it runs 3D2001, 3D2002, 3D2005, 3D2006. 3D2003 and 3D2004 do not exist. The reference file was correct to omit them — this gap is in the tariff, not the digitisation.

source_defects.schedule: Third Schedule: Stevedoring Charges
source_defects.note: The printed ordinals in section F jump from '5. TRANSHIPMENT' (3F5000) to '7. TRANSIT INBOUND' (3F6000) to '8. TRANSIT OUTBOUND' (3F7000). There is no ordinal 6. The CODES are sequential and unambiguous; only the printed ordinals skip.

source_defects.schedule: Third Schedule: Stevedoring Charges
source_defects.note: DUPLICATE CODES. This page numbers BIBO Operations 3L1008 (Stevedoring/Ship Operation, 0.36) and 3L1009 (Bagging Machine Operation, 1.35). Printed page 16 has ALREADY used 3L1008 (All Other Conventional Cargoes – Indirect Handling, 0.70) and 3L1009 (Dry Bulk Cargo (Grabbing), 0.70). Two different charges share each code. The existing digitisation disambiguated them as 3L1008b / 3L1009b, which is the right call — recorded here the same way, with the printed code preserved.

source_defects.schedule: Fourth Schedule: Receipt and Delivery Charges
source_defects.note: Section 4A2000's sub-headings run a, b, c then jump to 'f. DANGEROUS GOODS I'. Letters d and e are not used.

source_defects.schedule: Fourth Schedule: Receipt and Delivery Charges
source_defects.note: Section header is printed '1. TERMNAL HANDLING CHARGES' (missing the I in TERMINAL).

source_defects.schedule: Fourth Schedule: Receipt and Delivery Charges
source_defects.note: Two numbering skips in the PUBLISHED tables, not in the digitisation. 4D2000 Container Stuffing/Unstuffing runs 4D2001–4D2006 then jumps straight to 4D2019–4D2030; 4D2007–4D2018 do not exist. 4D3000 Re-Stuffing runs 4D3001–4D3003 then jumps to 4D3010–4D3015; 4D3004–4D3009 do not exist. The reference file was correct to omit all 18.

source_defects.schedule: Fourth Schedule: Receipt and Delivery Charges
source_defects.note: Two slips. (1) 4D4000 Partial Unstuffing runs 4D4001–4D4003 then jumps to 4D4010–4D4015; 4D4004–4D4009 do not exist in the published tariff. (2) The sub-section letters run a, then d, then e — b and c are skipped, where 4D2000 and 4D3000 on the previous page both use a, b, c for the same general-goods / DG I / DG II split.

source_defects.schedule: Fourth Schedule: Receipt and Delivery Charges
source_defects.note: Two slips on this page. (1) The running header reads 'C. CONTAINERS' but every code is 4D… — the section is D. Containers. (2) Within both 4D6000 and 4D7000 the sub-section letters run a, b, c and then 'b' AGAIN for Empty Containers, where d was intended.

source_defects.schedule: Fourth Schedule: Receipt and Delivery Charges
source_defects.note: 4D8000 labels its Empty Container block 'd' correctly; 4D9000 labels the equivalent block 'b' again, repeating the earlier b. Same slip seen on printed page 26.

source_defects.schedule: Fourth Schedule: Receipt and Delivery Charges
source_defects.note: Sub-section d. MISCELLANEOUS SERVICES prints 'GH¢' over ALL FOUR columns, including Transhipment and Transit. Every other table on this page and the surrounding pages prices those two columns in US$, and the magnitudes here (26.78 against 173.06) match the US$ pattern, not a cedi one. RESOLVED by the user 2026-08-09: USE THE TARIFF AS PRINTED — all four columns are GH¢. The observation is retained here as a note for anyone auditing an invoice against this line, but the data follows the printed document.

source_defects.schedule: Fourth Schedule: Receipt and Delivery Charges
source_defects.note: Sub-section 1. REMARKING prints column currencies as US$ | GH¢ | US$ | US$ and carries a value only in the Export (GH¢) column; the other three are '--'.

source_defects.schedule: Fourth Schedule: Receipt and Delivery Charges
source_defects.note: DUPLICATE CODES, second occurrence in the document. 4H1007 and 4H1008 are used for 'All Other Conventional Cargoes – Direct/Indirect Handling' (0.70) and then AGAIN immediately below for 'BIBO Operation – Direct/Indirect Handling' (1.39). This is the same failure seen at 3L1008/3L1009 on printed page 17. The existing digitisation disambiguated them as 4H1007b / 4H1008b, which is confirmed correct.

source_defects.schedule: Fourth Schedule: Receipt and Delivery Charges
source_defects.note: Section 4I0000's column headers read 'PER TONNE / PER TONNE' but its sub-section 2 (Handling of Livestock) re-labels them 'PER UNIT / PER UNIT'. The passenger rows are per tonne of baggage; livestock is per unit.

source_defects.schedule: Fifth Schedule: Hire of Craft and Equipment
source_defects.note: The printed table numbers the first Lighter/Barge row '7A7001'. That is a typo in the tariff itself — the section is 5A7000 and the run continues 5A7002…5A7008. Recorded here as 5A7001 with the printed form noted.

source_defects.schedule: Fifth Schedule: Hire of Craft and Equipment
source_defects.note: Section D rows are printed inconsistently as '5 D1001', '5 D0002', '5 D0003', '5 D0004' (stray space, and 1001 vs 0002 numbering). The section header is 5D1000, so they are recorded as 5D1001–5D1004.

source_defects.schedule: Fifth Schedule: Hire of Craft and Equipment
source_defects.note: The source numbers two consecutive sections '7' — 5H7000 'Fire Monitoring/Supervision' and 5H8000 'Takoradi Oil Jetty'. The codes are unambiguous; the printed ordinals are not.

source_defects.schedule: Fifth Schedule: Hire of Craft and Equipment
source_defects.note: DUPLICATE CODE, third occurrence in the document. '5I1062' is printed twice in succession — once for Safety Nets (6.80) and again for Salt Sling (2.97) — and 5I1061 is never used. The alphabetical run (Rubber boots, Safety Nets, Salt Sling, Shackles) shows Safety Nets should have been 5I1061. Recorded as printed with the intended code noted; NOT silently renumbered.

source_defects.schedule: Seventh Schedule: Tema Fishing Harbour Charges
source_defects.note: 7A1000 Berth Occupancy runs 7A1001, 7A1002, 7A1003 then jumps to 7A1006. Codes 7A1004 and 7A1005 do not exist. CONFIRMED FROM SOURCE — this matches the gap the detector flagged earlier and vindicates the reference for holding only four rows.

source_defects.schedule: Seventh Schedule: Tema Fishing Harbour Charges
source_defects.note: 7A4000 Mooring/Unmooring is headed 'PER GT US$'. At 42.42 per GT a 500 GT vessel would owe over US$21,000 to moor, which is implausible and inconsistent with every comparable table (2A4000 in the Second Schedule is Per Movement). The heading is almost certainly meant to read PER MOVEMENT. Recorded as printed with the doubt flagged — not silently corrected.

source_defects.schedule: Ninth Schedule: Oil and Gas Services Tariffs
source_defects.note: DUPLICATE CODE, fourth occurrence in the document. '9F2001' is printed twice in succession — Quay Apron/Marshalling Area (0.28 per hr) and Open Storage Area (0.33 per day) — and the run then continues 9F2002 for Covered Storage Area. The second and third rows are one number short throughout. This confirms the existing digitisation's 9F2001a / 9F2001b disambiguation as correct. Preserved as printed with the collision flagged.

source_defects.schedule: Tenth Schedule: Charges for Coastal Traffic
source_defects.note: DUPLICATE CODE, fifth occurrence in the document. '10A9011' is used for Trailer Units in sub-section III (1.88 / 5.60 / 5.60 per unit) and AGAIN for the PIDD per-vessel-call row in sub-section IV (0.20 per GT). Completely different charges, bases and columns. This confirms the existing digitisation's 10A9011b disambiguation as correct.

source_defects.schedule: Tenth Schedule: Charges for Coastal Traffic
source_defects.note: 10B4000 Mooring/Unmooring numbers its rows with FIVE digits — 10B40001 through 10B40006 — where every other section in this schedule uses four (10B3001, 10B5001, 10B6001). The extra zero is a printing inconsistency, not a different code family. Preserved as printed.

source_defects.schedule: Eleventh Schedule: Charges for Offshore Operations
source_defects.note: 11A1000 prints only 11A1001 (Light Dues) and 11A1004 (Anchorage Charges). 11A1002 and 11A1003 do not exist in the published tariff. The reference was correct to hold just the two.

source_defects.schedule: Eleventh Schedule: Charges for Offshore Operations
source_defects.note: 11A5000 skips 11A5014 — the printed table runs 11A5013 then 11A5015. That one number does not exist. Every other number 001–027 is printed.

source_defects.schedule: Twelfth Schedule: Ship Waste Reception Facilities (MARPOL 73/78) Charges
source_defects.note: 12A1001 is remarked 'Per Annum' while 12A1002 through 12A1005 are all 'Per Call'. Same table, same rate for the first two bands (1,050.00), but one is annual and the other per call — so a vessel up to 3,000 GT pays 1,050.00 once a YEAR while a vessel of 3,001 GT pays 1,050.00 EVERY CALL. RESOLVED by the user 2026-08-09: USE THE TARIFF AS PRINTED — 12A1001 is PER ANNUM. The cliff at 3,000 GT is real and must be honoured by the engine; do not normalise it to Per Call.

pricing_notes.schedule: Second Schedule: Vessel Handling Charges
pricing_notes.note: 2A1008 Baco Liner Barges is a berth-occupancy row the engine's RATES.berth table does not carry — its bands run on LOA only. Flag for the rewiring: a Baco Liner Barge call cannot currently be priced.

pricing_notes.schedule: Second Schedule: Vessel Handling Charges
pricing_notes.note: 2A6002 Anchorage for Oil Rigs and Production Platforms (0.02 / 0.01 / 0.008 / 0.006, min 300.00) is a SECOND anchorage band the engine does not carry — it prices only 2A6001 All Ships (0.01 → 0.005, min 250). Flag for the rewiring: an oil rig or production platform at anchorage is currently priced on the wrong band.

pricing_notes.schedule: Second Schedule: Vessel Handling Charges
pricing_notes.note: None of this page is priced by the engine today: Pilot Attendance (2B3001), movement to/from Tema Dry Dock (2C1001/2C1002), fresh water supply (2D1001-003) and under-water diver services (2D2001-004). Fresh water in particular is a routine agency line — worth surfacing as orderable services once the engine reads from the tariff.

pricing_notes.schedule: Third Schedule: Stevedoring Charges
pricing_notes.note: The Direct/Indirect +10% note is printed HERE, at the end of section A, and its wording is 'The rates specified for Conventional Cargoes UNDER THIS SCHEDULE are for Direct Handling'. It therefore governs all eight 3A blocks (3A1000–3A8000), not only Import. This confirms the propagation made on 2026-08-06 and closes the question left open on page 10.

pricing_notes.schedule: Third Schedule: Stevedoring Charges
pricing_notes.note: 3G1001/3G1002 Handling of Hatch Covers — 123.04 on board, 246.09 via quay, applicable to CONTAINER VESSELS ONLY. WIRED 2026-09-05 (v2.4.4, user: 'shifting hatch covers via onboard and ashore is in the tariffs'): on a container vessel the two ordered-service lines carry these codes and rates; on every other vessel they keep the MV MPP CLEO contractor rates (111.60 / 223.20) as instructed practice, code '-' — the tariff rows do not apply there, so the two price bases stay separated rather than conflated.

pricing_notes.schedule: Third Schedule: Stevedoring Charges
pricing_notes.note: Three craneage families the engine does not carry: 3H2004 Scrap Metal 6.68/t; 3H3001–3H3003 DRY BULK craneage at 1.32/t (grains/agri-bulks, chemicals, mineral ore — i.e. clinker and limestone, the commodities this agency handles most); and 3H5001–3H5003 ship-equipment craneage (hatch covers 33.08, trailer units 6.62, skips 6.62). The engine's craneage path is conventional-cargo only (3H2001-003) plus the 3H6001 minimum. A dry-bulk call using a GPHA crane is currently unpriceable.

pricing_notes.schedule: Third Schedule: Stevedoring Charges
pricing_notes.note: 3L1009 here is Dry Bulk Cargo (Grabbing) at 0.70 per tonne. RESOLVED ON PAGE 17: the tariff REUSES codes 3L1008 and 3L1009 for BIBO Operations with different rates (0.36 and 1.35). The engine's BIBO overtime at 1.35 matches that second 3L1009 exactly and is NOT a miscitation — the reconciliation check flagged it only because it compared against this first 3L1009. See p017.json.

pricing_notes.schedule: Third Schedule: Stevedoring Charges
pricing_notes.note: Whole families here the engine cannot price: 3I1001/3I1002 scrap metal discharge 30.43 / load 29.26 per tonne; 3I2001 pre-slinging 4.63 and 3I2002 palletisation 6.12; 3I3001-004 unpacked motor bikes; 3I4001/002 passenger baggage; 3I5001/002 livestock; 3I6001-003 ship equipment; 3J1001/002 documentation; 3K1001/002 BACO barge operations.

pricing_notes.schedule: Third Schedule: Stevedoring Charges
pricing_notes.note: 3L2001 Labour Delays/Idle Time/Stand-by is 8.00 per docker per hour and 3L2002 10.50 per support staff per hour. RESOLVED by the user 2026-08-09: the engine's 'Estimated Labour Delays' at 1% of stevedoring is the AGENCY'S OWN ESTIMATE, not a tariff figure — the two are different things and must both exist. The digitisation records the published 3L2001/3L2002 rates as printed; the agency estimate stays a separate line in the engine and is NOT to be replaced by them.

pricing_notes.schedule: Third Schedule: Stevedoring Charges
pricing_notes.note: This CORRECTS the note I wrote on p016.json. The engine's BIBO overtime line at 1.35 is NOT a miscitation — it matches the second 3L1009 (Bagging Machine Operation) exactly. The reconciliation check flagged it only because it compared against the first 3L1009. The engine is right; the tariff is ambiguous.

pricing_notes.schedule: Fourth Schedule: Receipt and Delivery Charges
pricing_notes.note: 4C1001 Receipt/Delivery of Dry Bulk Cargo by Terminal Conveyors, US$1.05 per tonne, applicable to Import, Export, Transhipment and Transit. A dry-bulk receipt/delivery line the engine has no path to.

pricing_notes.schedule: Fourth Schedule: Receipt and Delivery Charges
pricing_notes.note: The engine carries container THC as a family code '4D1' with a single value set. The published table is far richer: 4D1001–4D1034+ split by general goods / DG I / DG II, by Direct vs Indirect handling, by 20'/40'/45', and by stuffed vs OOG — each with four currency-distinct columns. The engine cannot currently reach OOG or the Indirect variants.

pricing_notes.schedule: Fourth Schedule: Receipt and Delivery Charges
pricing_notes.note: This page supplies the real codes behind three families the engine holds only as prefixes: 4D10 (Transport within Terminal), 4D11 (Additional Handling) and 4D12 (Lift-On Lift-Off). It also adds 4D13001-004, transfer of devanned vehicles within ICDs, which the engine has no path to.

pricing_notes.schedule: Fourth Schedule: Receipt and Delivery Charges
pricing_notes.note: The first two rows of this page carry NO code — they are the remaining tonnage tiers of 4G2015 (Transit, Conventional Cargo General), continuing from printed page 30. 4G2015 therefore has FIVE free-storage tiers, not three: up to 5,000 t = 21 days, 5,001-10,000 = 30, 10,001-15,000 = 40, 15,001-20,000 = 50, above 20,000 = 60. The daily rates 1.05 / 1.31 / 1.58 are constant across all five. This completes the row restored on p030.json.

pricing_notes.schedule: Fourth Schedule: Receipt and Delivery Charges
pricing_notes.note: 4H2001/4H2002 are the RECEIPT-AND-DELIVERY delay rates (8.40 / 11.03 per hour), distinct from the stevedoring delay rates 3L2001/3L2002 (8.00 / 10.50) on printed page 17. Two different published delay charges for two different operations — neither is the agency's own 1% estimate.

pricing_notes.schedule: Sixth Schedule: Charges for Small Craft
pricing_notes.note: Nothing in the Sixth Schedule is priced by the engine. It matters for the offshore work: part B covers craft in Ghanaian Territorial Waters, the EEZ and coastal waters for maritime security escort, security patrols and offshore support. Part B rates run roughly 1.4x to 6x part A — e.g. licence fees 5,250.00 against 871.42 for a craft up to 15 m. Note the explicit carve-out: part B does NOT apply to supply and support vessels deployed in oil and gas operations, which fall under Schedule 9.

pricing_notes.schedule: Seventh Schedule: Tema Fishing Harbour Charges
pricing_notes.note: Scope note worth carrying into the engine: this Schedule applies ONLY to GHANAIAN REGISTERED fish vessels calling at Tema Fishing Harbour. Foreign registered vessels at the Fishing Harbour, and Ghanaian fishing vessels at the main commercial ports, both pay the MAIN PORT tariffs instead. Choosing this schedule therefore depends on vessel registry as well as berth.

pricing_notes.schedule: Seventh Schedule: Tema Fishing Harbour Charges
pricing_notes.note: 7J1001 ISPS and 7K1001 PIDD are both 0.10 per GT per call with a US$25.00 MINIMUM — a different minimum from the main-port schedule (1J4000 ISPS carries a US$200 minimum). If the engine ever prices a fishing-harbour call it must use this minimum, not the main-port one.

pricing_notes.schedule: Eighth Schedule: Charges for Oil Rigs & Production Platforms
pricing_notes.note: None of the Eighth Schedule is priced by the engine. 8A3000 Towage is 'PER TUG HOUR PER GT' — a compound basis (tugs x hours x GT) unlike anything in the conventional schedules, and the engine has no shape for it. Note also 8A1004 Semi-Submersible Drill Craft berth occupancy is 1.00 per GT per day, DOUBLE the 0.50 that every other rig type pays; it is the only rate on the page that breaks the flat pattern.

pricing_notes.schedule: Eighth Schedule: Charges for Oil Rigs & Production Platforms
pricing_notes.note: Three conditional rules here that a data-driven engine must carry alongside the rates, because none of them is expressible as a rate alone: (1) lay-by charges DOUBLE after 90 days — 0.25 to 0.50 per GT per day for rigs, 0.50 to 0.75 for production platforms, so the charge depends on elapsed stay; (2) craft calling for LESS THAN 14 DAYS get a 50% rebate on ISPS Dues; (3) vessels calling at ANCHORAGE pay 50% of both ISPS and PIDD. The 90-day escalation in particular means a long rig lay-by cannot be priced by a single multiplication.

pricing_notes.schedule: Ninth Schedule: Oil and Gas Services Tariffs
pricing_notes.note: 9A2000 Port Dues on Cargo is the 21-row table the reference already held correctly and which the engine only reaches for three of (9A2001-003). The skip, container and basket rows 9A2004-9A2021 are all unreachable in the engine today. Note the exclusion: Liquid Bulk cargo here EXCLUDES MGO and bunker fuel supplied to Support/Supply Vessels via Tank Farms located in the Port — those go elsewhere, so a bunker movement must not be priced at 9.17/tonne.

pricing_notes.schedule: Ninth Schedule: Oil and Gas Services Tariffs
pricing_notes.note: 9B1000 Vessel Movement Charge is a COMPOSITE rate — one per-call figure covering Pilotage, Towage, Mooring/Unmooring AND Light Dues together. An oil and gas call must NOT be priced by summing the individual Second Schedule movement charges; that would multiply-count. Two riders attach: dumb barges pay DOUBLE the specified tariff, and pilotage of supply vessels calling the Naval Base is a flat US$200 per call regardless of size.

pricing_notes.schedule: Ninth Schedule: Oil and Gas Services Tariffs
pricing_notes.note: ISPS and PIDD here are 0.25 per GT per call with a US$100.00 minimum EACH — a third distinct minimum, after the main port's US$200 (1J4000) and the fishing harbour's US$25 (7J1000). Same charge name, three different floors depending on schedule.

pricing_notes.schedule: Ninth Schedule: Oil and Gas Services Tariffs
pricing_notes.note: A 25% REBATE applies where customers collect or deliver their consignments at the quayside with their own trucks. That is a conditional discount on every rate in this table, not a separate line — it depends on how the cargo interest moves the goods, which is exactly the operational fact the app has to ask about rather than infer.

pricing_notes.schedule: Ninth Schedule: Oil and Gas Services Tariffs
pricing_notes.note: INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION of the 11 rows restored on 2026-08-09 (9C1013–9C1023, the empty skips and all baskets) which the digitisation had dropped from the middle of this table. Re-read here from scratch in a separate pass, every figure matches the restoration exactly: 51.60 / 60.20 / 70.52 / 30.10 / 60.20 / 120.39 / 150.49 / 21.50 / 43.00 / 86.00 / 107.49.

pricing_notes.schedule: Ninth Schedule: Oil and Gas Services Tariffs
pricing_notes.note: The section note is a scope boundary the engine must respect: the rate INCLUDES cargo gears, labour, Tally, Condition Report and supervision, and EXCLUDES lifting equipment which is chargeable separately under 9E0000. So a 9C2 discharge must not also raise a separate tally or supervision line — but it MAY raise 9E dedicated equipment.

pricing_notes.schedule: Ninth Schedule: Oil and Gas Services Tariffs
pricing_notes.note: THE PAGE THAT STARTED THE REBUILD. 9C2010-9C2023 are the 14 skip and basket rows the digitisation had dropped and which the ENGINE had held correctly all along. Re-read here from scratch in an independent pass, all 14 match the engine and the restoration exactly: 407.09 / 508.86 / 534.30 / 63.61 / 76.33 / 89.05 / 38.16 / 76.33 / 114.49 / 152.66 / 22.26 / 44.53 / 63.61 / 89.05. Confirmed by three independent sources now — the engine constants, the first restoration, and this fresh reading.

pricing_notes.schedule: Ninth Schedule: Oil and Gas Services Tariffs
pricing_notes.note: 9C4001 Labour Delays for oil and gas is 11.03 per docker per hour — a FOURTH distinct delay figure, after 3L2001 (8.00, stevedoring), 4H2001 (8.40, receipt and delivery) and the agency's own 1% estimate. Same charge name, four different bases depending on which schedule the work falls under.

pricing_notes.schedule: Ninth Schedule: Oil and Gas Services Tariffs
pricing_notes.note: 9C3001 Lashing is 16.54 per man per hour, identical to the Third Schedule's 3M1001. Distinct again from the MV MPP CLEO contractor lashing the engine carries at 800/1,600 per shift — three different lashing bases now in play (GPHA conventional, GPHA oil and gas, contractor per shift).

pricing_notes.schedule: Ninth Schedule: Oil and Gas Services Tariffs
pricing_notes.note: TWO RULES THAT ARE NOT RATES. (1) Dedicated Equipment rates are inclusive of operator/driver, maintenance, lube oil and fuel BUT EXCLUSIVE of a GPHA charge of 20% of the chargeable rate, which must be ADDED and collected for GPHA. Every 9E figure is therefore 80% of what is actually billed. (2) A MINIMUM OF 2 HOURS applies to every mobile crane and forklift hire, so the per-hour column can never be multiplied by less than 2.

pricing_notes.schedule: Ninth Schedule: Oil and Gas Services Tariffs
pricing_notes.note: Two conditional rules attach: (1) Short Term Storage is a period NOT EXCEEDING 30 days; Long Term is a period EXCEEDING 30 days — so which table applies depends on elapsed dwell, and the same cargo crosses from one to the other. (2) Oil and gas cargo for shipment offshore or discharged from supply/support vessels must not stay on the quay apron beyond 8 HOURS; the Terminal Operator transfers it to the Common User Storage Area and the CARGO OWNER bears the transfer and storage cost. That 8-hour rule generates a charge automatically, so it is not optional.

pricing_notes.schedule: Tenth Schedule: Charges for Coastal Traffic
pricing_notes.note: Three rules that are not rates: (1) only RECIRCULATION empty containers apply to National Coastal Traffic (definition at Q41, page 77); (2) Feeder Service between TEMA AND TAKORADI gets a 5% REBATE on the regional feeder rates — directly relevant to a two-port Ghanaian call; (3) small craft licensed by the Authority as supply/support vessels are EXEMPT from port cleaning and light dues.

pricing_notes.schedule: Tenth Schedule: Charges for Coastal Traffic
pricing_notes.note: 10A8012 ISPS for passenger vessels and vessels not working cargo carries a US$100.00 MINIMUM and a 50% reduction for vessels calling at ANCHORAGE. That is the FOURTH distinct ISPS minimum in the document — main port US$200 (1J4000), fishing harbour US$25 (7J1000), oil and gas US$100 (9A4000), coastal US$100 (10A8012). The minimum is a property of the schedule, never of the charge name.

pricing_notes.schedule: Tenth Schedule: Charges for Coastal Traffic
pricing_notes.note: 10B6001 Anchorage carries a US$236.69 MINIMUM and a 50% REBATE for vessels spending no more than 24 hours at anchorage. That is a third anchorage minimum — main port 2A6001 is US$250 for all ships and 2A6002 is US$300 for oil rigs. Detention of pilot and cancellation at OFFSHORE locations attract DOUBLE the rates specified.

pricing_notes.schedule: Tenth Schedule: Charges for Coastal Traffic
pricing_notes.note: 10C3000 carries two conditional modifiers in its note: non-driveable vehicles attract an ADDITIONAL 25% of the rate specified, and a vehicle stuffed with goods or personal effects attracts ONE-HALF the rates specified. Those pull in opposite directions and both key off how the vehicle arrives, not what it is.

pricing_notes.schedule: Tenth Schedule: Charges for Coastal Traffic
pricing_notes.note: The three Empty DG Container rows 10C1013-10C1015 restored earlier were re-read here in a fresh pass and match exactly: 59.22/89.25/66.18, 106.23/160.09/124.76, 124.62/187.81/146.67.

pricing_notes.schedule: Twelfth Schedule: Ship Waste Reception Facilities (MARPOL 73/78) Charges
pricing_notes.note: The excess rules are separate charges, not part of the banded rate: additional garbage above 5 tonnes attracts US$10.00 per tonne, and oil/sludge above 25 tonnes attracts US$75.00 per tonne. The engine's MARPOL environmental charge uses the banded figure only.

rows.remarks: Applicable exclusively to vessels that did not load/discharge Cargo or Passengers during their call.

rows.remarks: Applicable exclusively to vessels that did not load/discharge Cargo or Passengers during their call.

sections.notes: Port Dues on Transhipment and Transit Inbound shall attract 60% of the rates specified here. | Takoradi refers to the Dry Bulk Terminal and Container Multipurpose Terminal (ATS).

sections.title: A. Small Craft Providing Services Within the Limit of the Port · 1. Licence Fees
sections.notes: For the purpose of this Schedule, a Small Craft is a craft that is licensed by GPHA to undertake operational activities within the limits of the ports. Operational activity here includes transport of crew, personnel, cargo, materials, stores, fuel, water, equipment, etc. All craft operating within the limits of the port, including the operators of such craft, shall be licensed by GPHA and their operations shall be limited to their own or agency vessels. Support and supply vessels operating in Ghanaian coastal waters i.e. outside the port limits shall be excluded from this Schedule. The applicable tariffs for such vessels are Schedule 9.

sections.title: B. Small Craft Providing Services Beyond the Limit of the Port · 1. Licence Fees
sections.notes: This part of the Port Tariffs is applicable to small Craft/Vessels deployed in Ghanaian Territorial Waters, Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) and Coastal Waters in services such as maritime security escort, maritime security patrols, and offshore support services. For the avoidance of doubt, these tariffs shall not apply to supply and support vessels deployed in oil and gas operations. The Owners of Craft/Vessels providing maritime security services must have entered into valid Agreement with the relevant state security agencies responsible for the development and deployment of maritime security forces, with the capability to ensure safe, secure and clean maritime domain of Ghana. Crafts/vessels deployed in other offshore operations shall be required to submit the permits from the GMA and other relevant regulatory agencies as may be required.

conditions.text: Port Dues is a charge for the use of the basic port infrastructure by vessels, cargo and passengers. The payment of Port Dues is to the account of the ship.
Port Dues on cargoes shipped between Tema and Takoradi shall be charged once only, in the Port of Loading.
The following are exempted from Port Dues on Cargo: Mails, Goods landed in error, Passengers under 3 years of age, pets, vessels under 100 gross tons.

Light Dues is a charge for the use of Navigational Aids and related facilities by vessels. It is payable in the first Ghanaian Port of call by deep sea vessels and is exhausted once the vessel leaves Ghanaian waters. Vessels operating in coastal waters pay light dues per month, except small craft licensed as Supply/Support Vessels.
Port Dues and other charges incurred by a vessel as a result of a detention order by a Court, Government Agency or other Legal Authority shall be borne by the Ship's Agent or Owner.
Port Dues on Cargo shall be assessed on the weight or Cubic Measurement (CBM), whichever is higher, where the goods are not in containers.
Port Dues on Unpacked Vehicles shall be assessed on the basis of the category (Car, Mini, Utility, etc.) of the vehicle.
Port Dues on Transhipment Unpacked Vehicles are for both Inbound and Outbound and shall be charged against the Inbound vessel only.
Port Dues on Cargo in Containers shall be assessed on the basis of the length of the Container (20', 40', 45').
Port dues on Transhipment Containers are for Inbound movement only. Outbound movement shall be charged separately at the same rate.

Port Dues on Vessels shall be assessed on the gross tons (GT). Applicable exclusively to vessels which did not work cargo nor embark/disembark passengers, save vessels under the Ninth Schedule which pay Port Dues on both vessels and cargo.

Vessels discharging/loading on a “free-in” or “free-out” basis may be billed for Port Dues on Cargo: 50% in US dollars; 50% may be converted to Ghana Cedi at the ruling rate on payment date. Invoices are debited to the accredited agent.

Exempted from Light Dues: (a) Vessels of less than 100 GT; (b) Vessels calling for Bunkers, Ship's Stores, Fresh Water for use on board; (c) Vessels in distress or calling for emergency repairs; (d) Vessels calling for medical assistance for the crew.
Exempted from Vessel Dues: (a) Vessels of less than 100 GT; (b) Vessels in distress or calling for emergency repairs; (c) Vessels calling for medical assistance for the crew.
Vessel Handling Charges (Marine Charges) include Pilotage, Towage, Mooring/Unmooring, Shifting, Berth Occupancy, etc. and are to the account of the ship.

The berthing of a vessel commences when the Pilot boards and ends when the first line is sent ashore to the bollard. Sailing starts when the first line is taken off the bollard and ends when the Pilot disembarks.
Normal pilotage uses one Pilot. Deployment of an additional pilot to assist normal vessel movement attracts 50% of the applicable Pilotage charge.

Shifting from one berth to another commences when the Pilot boards for the purpose of shifting and ends when the last line is fastened to the bollard. Shifting to the anchorage starts when the Pilot boards and ends when the Pilot disembarks.

Charges for Shifting are to the account of the vessel where the movement is at the Master's request or in pursuance of a Harbour Master's direction due to breach of a Port Regulation or performance standards.
Towage is compulsory for all vessels. One tug boat compulsory up to 10,000 GT and two tug boats above 10,000 GT. An extra tug boat attracts 50% Towage charge.
Vessels of 300m and above in LOA require a minimum of 3 tug boats for Towage.

Mooring/Unmooring charges apply to all vessels occupying a berth, buoy or mooring facility of the Authority, including private berths/wharves/anchorage/offshore facilities where Authority employees and craft are used.
Mooring/Unmooring operations include attendance to ropes and supply of necessary craft and Mooring Gangs/Crew.
Mooring/Unmooring charges apply to all vessels berthing alongside a quay, wharf, jetty, buoys or other mooring point, paid for each movement (Berthing, Sailing, Shifting, etc.).
Mooring/Unmooring at Offshore Locations (SPM, CBM, Oil Production Sites, etc.) attracts double the relevant rates.
The charge for Shifting of Vessels is inclusive of Towage, Pilotage and Mooring related to the movement.
Pilot Attendance is deployment of a Pilot for operations other than normal pilotage (e.g. Salvage, mid-stream and offshore cargo/survey operations).

Berth Occupancy Charge is assessed on the LOA range in metres as per Lloyd's Register of Shipping. It commences when the first line is sent ashore during berthing and ends when the last line is taken off the bollard when unberthing.

Pilotage is compulsory in all Pilotage Districts and shall be paid even if a Pilot is not deployed. All Supply/Support vessels moving in/out of the Sekondi Naval base must pay Pilotage to the Authority.
Pilotage, Towage, Mooring/Unmooring and Shifting charges are assessed on the GT range of the vessel/craft as per Lloyd's Register.
Pilotage, Towage and Mooring/Unmooring of a vessel not under steam (stalled/dead engine) or in distress attract double the relevant rates.
For a vessel berthing successively at several berths during a call, the time from mooring at the first berth to unmooring at the last is one continuous berthing duration for Berth Occupancy.
A vessel/craft using the anchorage at the request of the Authority (e.g. temporary unavailability of a berth, bad weather) is exempt from Anchorage Charges.

A vessel intending to use the anchorage other than at the Authority's request must apply via the “Application to Use Anchorage” form ahead of arrival or within 12 hours of arrival. Failure attracts a fine of US$5,000.00 plus accrued charges. Vessels without an accredited local agent are denied use of the anchorage.

Authority permission must be sought before a private company provides under-water services in the Port. Failure to seek written approval attracts a penalty of US$10,000.00. Where a private company provides the service, it pays 25% of fees charged as Royalty to the Authority.
Where charges are assessed on weight, the higher of CBM or deadweight Tonne applies. A Tonne equals 1,000 kg or one cubic meter (CBM).
Where minimum charge does not apply, charges are calculated to the nearest Tonne (e.g. 5.2 tonnes → 5 tonnes; 5.5 tonnes → 6 tonnes).
Heavy lifts are charged using CBM or deadweight, whichever yields higher revenue. For conventional cargo, heavy lift rates apply where deadweight is used as the basis.
For Oil and gas cargo, heavy lift rates (6–10t, above 10 up to 20t, and above 20t) apply where deadweight is the basis.
If CBM is used as the basis for charging heavy lifts (per C3 and C4), the standard rate (lifts up to 5 tonnes) is used.

Cargo handling rates apply to normal working hours. Overtime attracts additional charges — assessed by cargo volume for stevedoring/ship-related shore operations, and by persons deployed × overtime hours for storage-related shore operations.
Where additional services are required, additional charges cover the reasonable cost of services provided.
Fertilizers (including in containers) shipped for agricultural purposes are exempt from the dangerous cargo rate and charged as non-hazardous (general) goods, including transit cargo.
Live animals shall be delivered/shipped per the direct route at all times. The receiver provides feed, water and other needs.
The cargo receiver/shipper supplies, at no cost to the Stevedore, the grabs, hoppers and other dry bulk handling equipment for loading/discharging Dry Bulk and Semi-Bulk cargoes.

All heavy-duty equipment not normally plying public roads (metal-tracked, earth moving, mining dump trucks, pay loaders, crawlers, rollers, mobile cranes, compressors, asphalt machines, mobile generators, etc.) is treated as conventional cargo.
All automobiles intended to carry goods/personnel that normally ply public roads (cars, vans, buses, agricultural tractors, construction dump trucks) are treated as Unpacked Vehicles.
Vehicles/Trailers in stacks of more than one, stuffed with other vehicles/trailers, attract rates per the vehicle/trailer type for the number in the stack.
Vehicles stuffed with personal effects or goods (other than vehicle accessories) attract one-half of the applicable rates.
Trailers stuffed with goods (e.g. knocked-down vehicle parts, machinery, tyres) attract one-half of the charge.
Vehicles stacked on trailers attract the appropriate charge for the vehicle type.
Vehicles/Trailers stuffed with knocked-down components or units of machinery/equipment are considered stuffed vehicles.
Articulated vehicles are charged as two units — a utility vehicle and a trailer unit.
Stevedorage, Craneage, Labour and Terminal Handling Charges of Transhipment Unpacked Vehicles are for both Inbound and Outbound, charged against the Inbound vessel only.
Dangerous Goods Group I shall not be stored in the Port — routed through direct mode at all times.
Transhipment containers with Dangerous Goods are routed through direct ship-to-ship mode at all times and not stored in the port.

The owner of a container RO-RO vessel carrying containers/project cargo must maintain appropriate cargo handling equipment on the ship for Licensed Stevedores; such use attracts no charge from the ship.
Where such a vessel lacks appropriate equipment, Stevedores charge the ship at the Craneage rate for all containers moved across the ramp using their equipment.
Stevedores make no payments to the ship for use of ship equipment (cranes, derricks, lift trucks, tractor-trailer sets, gears, etc.), including equipment maintained on RO-RO vessels.
Stevedorage, Craneage, Labour and Terminal Handling Charges of Transhipment Containers are for Inbound only. Outbound movement charged separately at the same rate.
Transhipment Container volumes attract Rebate on Port Dues, Stevedorage and Terminal Handling Charges after attaining a throughput of 25,000 TEUs per annum, granted per the Rebate table.

conditions.section: D. Assignment of Cranes and Craneage
conditions.text: The Authority and its Licensed Operators/Concessionaires reserve the right to assign a Quay Crane or Mobile Harbour Crane to expedite operations; such deployment attracts appropriate Craneage.

conditions.section: D. Assignment of Cranes and Craneage
conditions.text: Craneage is in addition to the Stevedoring and Labour Overtime Charges. It is to the account of the ship.

conditions.section: D. Assignment of Cranes and Craneage
conditions.text: A minimum Craneage Charge applies when cargo volume during a ship call is low and total Craneage income is less than the minimum specified per crane.

conditions.section: D. Assignment of Cranes and Craneage
conditions.text: Craneage is only applicable when a crane is deployed as part of Stevedoring Operations.
Labour Charges cover Overtime, Stand-By, Idle Time and Extra Service for Ship Operations and Receipt & Delivery Operations.
Labour Charges for Ship Related Shore Activities (Overtime, Delay/Idle Time, Stand-by, Extra Service) apply to Imports, Exports, Transhipment and Transit, and are to the account of the ship.
Labour Overtime for ship-related shore activities is determined by cargo nature and volume (tonnage/unit/TEU), applicable whether or not the vessel works during overtime hours.
Labour Delays/Idle Time/Standby hours in ship-related activities during overtime hours are logged and invoiced.
Labour Standby Charges (ship-related) are raised when labour is deployed during both normal duty and overtime hours on customer request.
Labour Charges for storage-related shore activities apply to both Receipt and Delivery of Cargo and to all trade categories; to the account of the Consignee.
Labour Overtime for storage-related activity is assessed on persons deployed (with prior agreement) and actual overtime hours; to the account of the Cargo Receiver/Consignee.

Overtime hours for stevedoring (incl. ship-related receipt/delivery): Mon–Fri Day Shift 1230–1400 and 1700–1930 GMT, Night Shift 0330–0730 GMT; Sat/Sun/Public Holiday Day 0730–1930, Night 1930–0730 GMT.
Overtime hours for Receipt & Delivery (storage-related): Mon–Sat Day 1530–1930, Night 0330–0730 GMT; Sun/Public Holiday Day 0730–1930, Night 1930–0730 GMT.
Cargoes shifted via quay or on board, and those landed in error by the stevedore, are exempt from Labour Overtime Charge.

Extra Service charge applies when labour is deployed for jobs ancillary to stevedoring (trimming dry bulk, salvage of damaged cargo, stuffing/unstuffing, cleaning hatches, laying dunnage). Based on actual men deployed.
In Receipt & Delivery, Extra Service applies for ancillary shore activities (salvage, weighing, bagging spilled cargo, etc.).
When labour is booked exclusively for extra service, the minimum chargeable time is 8 hours.
Preparation of Vehicle Condition Reports (VCRs) and vehicle-handling documentation is integral to handling and does not attract the Extra Service Charge.

Hire of Labour (Non-Stevedoring) applies to activities unrelated to traditional stevedoring/shore-handling. The hirer is responsible for deployment, supervision and any liability arising from the persons employed.
Terminal Handling, Storage and Transport charges on Empty Containers are to the account of the ship's agent.
The Terminal Handling Charge for Transhipment Containers is for one leg of the shipment.
The charge for Evacuation of Empty Containers does not include Lift-On-Lift-off Charge at the destination.
Storage rent on inbound containers/cargo (Imports, Transhipment Inbound, Transit Inbound) is computed from the date of completion of discharge to the date of delivery.
Storage rent on Export containers/cargo is computed from the date of receipt in the Port to the date of loading onto the carrying vessel.

Where a vessel's operation is disrupted (shifted to anchorage, equipment breakdown, dispute, etc.), storage rent days for discharged cargo commence from the last day of operation prior to the disruption.
For import containers unstuffed in the Port/ICD, storage rent on the Empty Container is computed from the date it was unstuffed to the date of evacuation or shipment.

Cargoes consolidated for Export (incl. empty containers) but later removed from the Port attract full storage rent for the period spent, plus relevant Receipt & Delivery Charges, with no rent-free days.
Empty Containers imported to ship Export cargoes but later shipped as Empties enjoy a 7-day storage rent-free period.
Transit Containers attract no rebate on storage charges when empty and are invoiced as though they were Exports.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: Hiring of any plant/equipment commences from the time it leaves its station until its return; may be waived/modified under special circumstances (distance, duration, etc.).

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: Hire of GPHA-owned Floating Craft or Cargo Handling Equipment is at the absolute discretion of GPHA, which may require additional insurance conditions.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: Equipment hired out shall not be transferred by the Hirer to another party.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: Hire charges apply irrespective of whether the service is rendered during weekday, weekend, public holiday, day or night.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: “Within Port” (floating craft) = enclosed Harbour Basin and locations within the Anchorage Area; “Outside Port” = locations beyond the Anchorage Area. For cargo handling equipment in Tema, “Within Port” = area bordered by Meridian Road and the Tema Fishing Harbour Road; in Takoradi, within the port perimeter fence.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: The equipment hire charge includes the operational and technical crew.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: Minimum hire for floating craft: 2 hours (Within Enclosed Water Area), 3 hours (Within Anchorage Area), 4 hours (Beyond Anchorage – Offshore). A 2-hour charge is raised when a confirmed booking is cancelled before work begins.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: Minimum hire for cargo handling equipment: 4 hours (Outside Port), 2 hours (Within Port). A 2-hour charge applies for cancelled confirmed bookings.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: The hirer cannot transfer or sub-hire equipment to third parties without the owner's written consent.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: The charge for hire of the Diving Pontoon includes the use of on-board equipment.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: The charge for deployment of the underwater camera includes the Diver.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: For floating craft, the hiring period commences when the craft leaves its mooring and ceases when it returns. The charge is payable whether or not the purpose of hiring was effected.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: Hire of craft for salvage operations (towage of dead vessels, assisting vessels in distress, etc.) attracts double the Fifth Schedule rates. Also applies to Tug Boats assisting Floating Storage Units (FSUs) at midstream/anchorage/offshore.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: The craft and appurtenances are presumed seaworthy when turned over, but the Authority does not warrant mechanical condition and accepts no responsibility for delays from any cause.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: The Authority reserves the right to stop the operation of any craft to require repairs it deems necessary.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: The hirer/user assumes sole responsibility and liability for injury/death or property damage arising from possession, use or operation of the craft, and shall indemnify the Authority, its officers and employees.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: Hire of fire-fighting equipment to any offshore facility attracts double the rates. Minimum hire: 2 hours Within Port, 4 hours Outside Port.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: Hire of Fire Fighting Equipment for vessel-related Stand-by/Attendance/Monitoring commences from berthing until sailing.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: The cost of chemical used in fire-fighting is charged separately.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: Hire charges for floating craft and equipment apply irrespective of weekday, weekend, public holiday, day or night.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: All gears supplied are deemed in good order and returned in safe, clean, sound condition. Damaged gears are repaired/replaced by the Hirer.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: The number of pumps required for standing by or fire attendance is determined by the Fire Manager.

conditions.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
conditions.text: Hire of Grabs, Container Spreaders and Cargo Handling Gears to a location outside the Port attracts double the scheduled rates.

conditions.section: H. Licence Fees for Small Craft
conditions.text: Licence Fees and Dues for Small Craft, Supply and Support Vessels are annual charges applying to individual licensed vessels/craft. The operator must be licensed as a “Small Vessel/Craft Operator”.
A maximum of four packages not exceeding a total of 50 kg is exempt from charges. Excess baggage is chargeable per tariff.

The Authority is not liable for loss, mis-delivery, detention or damage to goods in transit areas, except where caused by want of reasonable foresight and care by the Authority or its servant. Independent contractors are not servants of the Authority.
Charges for logs and curls are payable by contracting agents on behalf of the owner, on the tonnage shown on the ship's manifest.
Storage rent on rejected logs is payable by contracting agents on behalf of the owner.

conditions.section: L. Removal of Goods Detained by Customs
conditions.text: Goods shall not remain in a transit storage facility beyond 60 days (subject to Customs & Excise Regulations) from completion of discharge. Overstayed goods are moved to the State Warehouse/designated facilities; goods entered at Customs may be auctioned by Customs.

conditions.section: L. Removal of Goods Detained by Customs
conditions.text: Any expenses incurred by the Authority in such removal or sales are a charge against the goods.

conditions.section: L. Removal of Goods Detained by Customs
conditions.text: The Authority accepts no liability for loss, damage or deterioration of goods transferred to the State Warehouse, Government Warehouse, Back Sheds, Overstayed Container Terminals, etc.

conditions.section: L. Removal of Goods Detained by Customs
conditions.text: The Authority is not responsible for goods detained by Customs or other authorities for examination, testing, treatment, fumigation, destruction, etc. Expenses are a charge against the owner of the goods.

conditions.section: M. Maximum Storage Period of Empty Containers
conditions.text: The maximum storage period for any empty container is 90 days from date of receipt or the date it became empty. After 90 days, the container is impounded and legal procedures commence for disposal by auction to defray costs.

conditions.section: N. Conversion of US Dollars to Ghana Cedis
conditions.text: Unless otherwise specified, where agreement is approved to charge a US-dollar tariff in Ghana Cedi, the cedi charge is at the rate of exchange on the date of payment.
Any transhipment container whose contents are unstuffed or re-packaged in the Port loses the concessionary transhipment rates and is charged as Import for the inbound and Re-export for the outbound.

It is the duty of the agent of the carrier/cargo to ensure the compressor and refrigeration system of a Reefer Container is in perfect working condition at all times. GPHA is not liable for any malfunctioning that might affect the condition of the content.

The Agent of the carrier vessel is responsible for payment of all charges (electricity, handling, storage, etc.) that accrue on a Reefer Container not claimed or cleared, or whose contents are due for destruction by Customs, Port Health, etc.

Additional Handling of Container: handling not directly connected to loading, discharging, receiving or delivering (e.g. truck-to-truck transfer at consignee's instance; re-evacuation of short-shipped containers). Quay transfer during ship operation/stevedoring is excluded.
Additional Sorting: sorting of consignments/packages to consignees' marks, numbers, drop numbers, etc.
Bulk Carriers: vessels designed to carry dry bulk cargoes, including Container-Bulk Carriers (Con-Bulkers). Vessel Handling Charges apply irrespective of cargo carried.
Bulk-In-Bagged-Out (BIBO): an operation in which cargo arrives in bulk and is bagged at shipside. The shore operator transfers indirect-routed BIBO into storage.
Bulk Cargo — Grabbing/Conveyor: dry bulk cargoes loaded with grabs, hoppers, pneumatic or continuous handling systems.

Coastal Traffic: short sea shipping in Ghanaian/West African waters. National Coastal — cargo produced/imported and cleared for consumption in Ghana, shipped between Ghanaian ports on a licensed vessel (incl. recirculation empties). Intra-regional — cargo traded among ECOWAS countries. Regional Feeder — cargo carried inbound on deep sea vessels and transhipped from Ghanaian ports to other ECOWAS ports.

Containers: ISO and Non-ISO units; Flats, Platforms, Bolsters. 20ft = up to 20ft; 40ft = above 20ft up to 40ft; 45ft = above 45ft up to 53ft. 45ft and above 40ft are deemed 2.5 TEUs for billing. Excludes Skips, accommodation units, goose necks, ro-ro trailers and other wheeled units.
Direct Handling: continuous handling between ship and inland conveyance where cargo does not undergo intermediate transit storage.

Dangerous Goods (DGs): substances per SOLAS 1974 / IMDG Code and MARPOL Annexes. DG Group I = IMDG Classes 1 (Explosives), 2 (Flammable & Poisonous Gases), 5 (Oxidizing Substances & Organic Peroxides), 7 (Radioactive Substances). DG Group II = IMDG Classes 3, 4, 6, 8, 9. Container DG I = Classes 1,2,5,7 (direct route at all times). Container DG II = Classes 3,4,6,8,9 (limited time in Port). Mixed goods → charged as DG.
Direct Transhipment: handling/movement of cargo from inbound to outbound vessel at the same time, without intermediate storage.
Dirty Cargoes: cargoes that mess up/foul quay aprons, storage and operational areas during handling, or emit dust particles.
Dump Barge: a barge that is not self-propelled and is moved by a tug boat.
Exports: produce of Ghana for shipment to foreign markets (traditional and non-traditional commodities).
Failure to Report for Delivery: charge applicable to consignees/agents who fail to report after a container is scheduled and positioned for delivery.
Fire Attendance: response of fire tender and crew to fire incidents.
Fire Stand-by: deployment of fire equipment and crew to mitigate fire threats.
Fire Safety Dues: dues for the use of in-built fire suppression systems installed at Liquid Bulk Terminals.
Fire/Safety Monitoring and Supervision: deployment of fire equipment/crew to provide technical advice and supervise client operations.
General Port Cleaning Dues: a general charge for cleaning the port, assessed against all dry bulk and dirty cargoes; to the account of the ship.
Gross Tonnage (GT) of Vessel: measured per the International Convention of Tonnage Measurement of Ships (1969), effective 18 July 1994.
Indirect Handling: handling between ship and inland conveyance involving routing through transit storage.
Indirect Transhipment: handling/movement of cargo from inbound vessel into transit storage for later shipment on an outbound vessel.

Inland Clearance Depots (ICDs): terminals (Off Dock Terminals) licensed to provide Receipt, Delivery and Shipment Services for Containers and Vehicles (e.g. Safebond, Tema Container Terminal, TBT, TACOTEL, etc.).
ICD Handling Charge: a charge for delivering inbound (import/transit-in) container to a consignee.
Inter-Terminal Transfer: movement of containers/vehicles/cargoes from one on-dock terminal to another. Transfer between two licensed ICDs uses the same rate as Terminal 1↔2.
ISPS Dues: charge for implementing the International Ship and Port Security Code (SOLAS Ch. XI-2, in force July 2004); to the account of the ship.
Layby Charges: applicable to Oil Rigs, Production Platforms and similar craft stemmed at mid-stream undergoing repairs/maintenance.
Length-Over-All (LOA): the length of a vessel in metres from extreme point forward to extreme point aft, as per Lloyd's Register.

Lift-On-Lift-Off of Container: relates to ICDs/Depot and involves loading a container from a truck where the customer provides the truck and the Terminal Operator provides equipment. Does not apply when THC is raised.
Lift-On/Lift-Off Operation: stevedoring using ship's cranes, derricks and quayside cranes. Vehicles/Trailers by Lo-Lo attract 25% surcharge above Ro-Ro stevedoring rates.
Light Dues: general charges for use of navigational aids; to the account of the ship.
Oil Terminal Loading Arm Dues: a general charge for use of Loading Arms at the Oil Terminals; to the account of the ship.
Opening of Containers: cutting security seals and opening for sighting or sampling only, without labour/equipment. If labour/equipment removes part of the content, Partial Unstuffing Charge applies.

Out of Gauge (OOG) Container: a container loaded above the top casting or beyond its length/width, requiring special spreader attachments or manual slings (flats, open tops stuffed above casting level, stuffed bolsters, damaged/warped/hogged containers, and those needing spreader extensions).
Over-Stayed Container Terminal: a GPHA-licensed facility for receipt, storage, auctioning and delivery of Overstayed Import Containers (containers designated for auction by Ghana Customs).

Partial Unstuffing Charge: for removal of part of a container's content for customs examination or security control; includes re-stuffing; in addition to the Terminal Handling Charge; to the account of the consignee/shipper.
Pipeline Dues: charges for use of pipelines connecting port terminals and tank farms (incl. the Tema Oil Refinery); to the account of the cargo owner.
Port Infrastructure Development Dues (PIDD): a special port due for financing future Port Infrastructure Development Projects, levied on all cargo and vessels; to the account of the ship.
Re-Circulation Empty Containers: empty containers that arrived as stuffed boxes and were later emptied (unstuffing into CFS, delivery to consignees, or shipment as break bulk).

Re-Exports: cargoes brought in under temporary arrangements (exhibition, samples, construction projects) shipped back to origin/third countries, or imports/transhipment re-packaged in the Port for shipment by sea. Charged as EXPORTS.

Restuffing Charge: packing cargoes that have been unstuffed (fully or partially) back into containers. Additional to the unstuffing charge (except partial unstuffing); to the account of the consignee/shipper.
Roll-On/Roll-Off (RO-RO) Operation: stevedoring operation on a Ro-Ro vessel.
Semi-Bulk [Grabbing]: use of grab/conveyors/continuous systems to load bulk cargoes emptied/bled from bags at shipside.
Semi-Bulk [Bleeding]: cutting open bagged cargoes and emptying contents as bulk at the shore or into cargo holds.
Stevedoring: handling/movement of cargo between the ship's hold and the storage area (and vice versa), incl. stacking/de-stacking. To the account of the ship.
Stuffing and Unstuffing Charge: removal of container contents or packing of cargoes into containers, separate from the Terminal Handling Charge; to the account of the consignee/shipper.
Support Staff: Terminal Clerks, Foremen, Supervisors, Plant Operators, etc.
State Warehouse (SWH): a customs-bond warehouse for cargoes un-entered at Customs or unclaimed after 30 days of the carrying vessel's departure.

Terminal Handling Charge (THC): charge for delivering/receiving a container to/from a consignee/shipper or ICD, covering handling and movement between storage and delivery/receipt point. Applies to outbound containers, vehicles and general cargo; excludes packing/removal of contents. Empty container THC paid by the Shipping Line.

Transhipment: cargoes using Port facilities but destined for other countries, moving on the second leg by sea. Manifested as such on arrival. Except DG containers for TBT, transhipment cargo shall not leave the Port through landside gates. Unstuffed/re-packaged transhipment loses the rate and is charged as Import + Re-Export.

Transit Cargo: cargoes using Port facilities but destined for other countries, transported by inland modes (road, rail, inland waterway). Manifested/declared as such at arrival. Transit rates do not apply to empty containers.
Transport of Containers within Terminal: movement of containers within the same terminal; applicable to on-dock Terminal operations only.
Transfer of Containers/Unpacked Vehicles from Port to ICDs: movement of containers, vehicles and other cargoes from the Ports to any Licensed ICD.
Truck Waiting Fees: a charge for consignees/agents unable to process enough container loads to fill their trucks, where the partially loaded truck remains at the Delivery Bay awaiting a top-up.
Tonne: 1,000 kg or one cubic meter (CBM); the higher of weight or CBM is used to invoice. Iron and Steel Products (incl. steel pipes) are always invoiced using the higher of weight or CBM.
Unitised Cargo: Palletised Cargo, Pre-Slung Cargo, Jumbo Bags and Paper Reels. Excludes Bundled and Coiled Cargo (steel, lumber, etc.).

Unpacked Vehicles: vehicles shipped on their wheels (Saloon cars, Mini Buses, Vans, Station Wagons, Cross Country Vehicles, Pickups, Tipper Trucks). Categories: Saloon/Estate (cabs up to 2t, up to 5 persons, incl. tri-cycles/aboboya); Mini (Mini Buses, Vans, Pick-ups, Cross Country, Station Wagons, above 2t up to 3t); Utility (Buses, Trucks, Road Tractors, Agricultural Tractors); Trailer Units; Driveable/Non-Driveable; Stuffed Vehicles; Machinery/Equipment (treated as conventional); Rollable Machinery; Devanned (Containerised) Vehicles (no THC after devanning, but attract Transfer and Storage at Unpacked Vehicle rates).
Charges are for implementing Annex I and V of the IMO MARPOL 73/78 Convention. Payable by all vessels calling at the Port save those exempt.

2A1001.description: All Vessels — LOA is Up to 150 Metres
2A1001.notes: Vessels which spend 6 hours or less in Port shall enjoy a 50 percent rebate on Berth Occupancy Charge. | A Vessel which calls at the Port for the sole purpose of loading fresh water, bunkers, stores, or pick/disembark crew and spends six hours or less shall be granted 50 per cent rebate on the Berth Occupancy Charge. | Any Vessel occupying a commercial berth for reasons other than cargo works e.g. breakdown, repairs, striking crew, etc. shall attract a surcharge of $5,000 per day of 24 hours or part thereof. | The following items/events are exempted from payment of Berth Occupancy Charge: (a) Time spent by a vessel in Port on Christmas Day and Good Friday; (b) A Ship which fails to sail due to causes for which the Vessel is not responsible, and which the Harbour Master has certified that the delay in sailing was in the interest of the Port; (c) Ships berthing at the VALCO Berth at Tema.

6A1001.section: A. Small Craft Providing Services Within the Limit of the Port · 1. Licence Fees
6A1001.notes: For the purpose of this Schedule, a Small Craft is a craft that is licensed by GPHA to undertake operational activities within the limits of the ports. Operational activity here includes transport of crew, personnel, cargo, materials, stores, fuel, water, equipment, etc. All craft operating within the limits of the port, including the operators of such craft, shall be licensed by GPHA and their operations shall be limited to their own or agency vessels. Support and supply vessels operating in Ghanaian coastal waters i.e. outside the port limits shall be excluded from this Schedule. The applicable tariffs for such vessels are Schedule 9.

6B1001.schedule: Sixth Schedule: Charges for Small Craft
6B1001.section: B. Small Craft Providing Services Beyond the Limit of the Port · 1. Licence Fees
6B1001.notes: This part of the Port Tariffs is applicable to small Craft/Vessels deployed in Ghanaian Territorial Waters, Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) and Coastal Waters in services such as maritime security escort, maritime security patrols, and offshore support services. For the avoidance of doubt, these tariffs shall not apply to supply and support vessels deployed in oil and gas operations. The Owners of Craft/Vessels providing maritime security services must have entered into valid Agreement with the relevant state security agencies responsible for the development and deployment of maritime security forces, with the capability to ensure safe, secure and clean maritime domain of Ghana. Crafts/vessels deployed in other offshore operations shall be required to submit the permits from the GMA and other relevant regulatory agencies as may be required.

terms_source_pages.title: General Terms and Conditions — printed page 64
terms_source_pages.searchable_transcription:
GENERAL TERMS AND CONDITIONS

A. PORT DUES

1. Port Dues is a charge for the use of the basic port infrastructure by vessels, cargo and passengers. The payment of Port
Dues is to the account of the ship.

2. Port Dues on cargoes shipped between Tema and Takoradi shall be charged once, i.e. only, in the Port of Loading.

Oo

The following are exempted from Port Dues on Cargo: Mails, Goods landed in error, Passengers under 3 years of age,
pets, vessels under 100 gross tons.

4. Light Dues is a Charge for the use of Navigational Aids and related facilities and services by vessels. It is payable in
the first Ghanaian Port of call by deep sea vessels calling in Ghana; and it is exhausted once the vessel leaves Ghanaian
waters. Vessels operating in the coastal waters of Ghana shall pay light dues on a per month basis, except small craft
licensed by the Authority to operate as Supply/Support Vessels.

5. Port Dues and other charges incurred by a vessel as a result of a detention order by a Court, a Government Agency or
any other Legal Authority shall be borne by the Ships’ Agent or Owner.

6. Port Dues on Cargo shall be assessed on the weight or Cubic Measurement (CBM) of the cargo whichever is higher,
where the goods are not in containers.

7. Port Dues on Cargo on Unpacked Vehicles shall be assessed on the basis of the category (i.e. Car, Mini, Utility, etc.)
of the vehicle.

8. Port Dues on Transhipment Unpacked Vehicles are for both Inbound and Outbound and shall be charged against the
Inbound vessels only.

9. Port Dues on Cargo in Containers shall be assessed on the basis of the length of the Container (20’, 40’, 45’).

10. Port dues on Transhipment Containers are for Inbound movement only. Outbound movement shall be charged
separately at the same rate.

11. Port Dues on Vessels shall be assessed on the gross tons (GT) of the vessel. It is applicable exclusively to vessels
which did not call to work cargo nor embark/disembark passengers, save vessels applicable under the Ninth Schedule
— Oil and Gas Services which shall pay Port Dues on both vessels and cargo.

12. Vessels discharging or loading cargo on a “free-in” or “free-out” basis may be billed for Port Dues on Cargo as follows:
a. 50% of Port Dues on Cargo assessed in US dollars shall be paid in US dollars.

b. 50% of Port Dues on Cargo assessed in US dollars may be converted into Ghana Cedi at the ruling exchange
rate on the date of payment of the invoice.

c. Invoices raised against such vessels will be debited to the account of the accredited agent of the vessel.
13. The following are exempted from payment of Light Dues:
Vessels of less than 100 GT
Vessels calling for Bunkers, Ship’s Stores, Fresh Water for use on board

Vessels in distress or calling for emergency repairs
Vessels calling for medical assistance for the crew

aege

terms_source_pages.title: General Terms and Conditions — printed page 65
terms_source_pages.searchable_transcription:
14. The following are exempted from payment of Vessel Dues:

a. Vessels of less than 100 GT
b. Vessels in distress or calling for emergency repairs
c. Vessels calling for medical assistance for the crew.

B. VESSEL HANDLING

1.

Vessel Handling Charges - also called Marine Charges - include Pilotage, Towage, Mooring/Unmooring, Shifting,
Berth Occupancy, etc. and are to the account of the ship.

The berthing of a vessel commences when the Pilot boards the vessel and ends when the first line is sent ashore to be
fastened to the bollard. Sailing of a vessel starts when the first line is taken off the bollard and ends when the Pilot
disembarks.

. Normal pilotage operation shall be performed using one Pilot. The deployment of additional pilot to assist normal vessel

movement shall attract 50% of the applicable Pilotage charge for the vessel.

Shifting of a vessel from one berth to another commences at the exact time the Pilot boards the vessel for the purpose
of shifting the vessel and ends when the last line is fastened to the bollard. Shifting of a vessel from one berth to the
anchorage starts when the Pilot boards the vessel and ends when the Pilot disembarks.

The charge for Shifting of a Vessel from one berth to another or to the anchorage are to the account of the vessel where
the movement is made at the request of the Master of the ship, or it is in pursuance of a direction given by the Harbour
Master because the ship is in breach of a Port Regulation or performance standards.

Towage is compulsory for all vessels calling at the Port. Towage with one Tug Boat is compulsory for all vessels up to
10,000 GT and two Tug Boats for vessels above 10,000 GT. The deployment of an extra Tug boat shall attract 50%
Towage charge applicable to the vessel.

Vessels of 300m and above in length — LOA, shall require a minimum of 3 Tug boats for Towage.
Mooring/Unmooring charges shall apply to all vessels occupying a berth, buoy or any mooring facility belonging to the
Authority. It shall also apply to private berths, wharves, anchorage or offshore facilities where Authority employees

and craft are utilized.

Mooring/Unmooring operations includes attendance to ropes and the supply of necessary craft and Mooring
Gangs/Crew.

10. Mooring/Unmooring charges shall be applicable to all vessels berthing alongside a quay, wharf, jetty, buoys or other

mooring point. It shall be paid for each movement i.e. Berthing, Sailing, Shifting, etc.

11. Mooring/Unmooring of vessel/craft at Offshore Locations e.g. SPM, CBM, Oil Production Sites, etc. shall attract double

the relevant rates specified in the Tariffs.

12. The charge for Shifting of Vessels is inclusive of Towage, Pilotage, and Mooring related to the movement of the vessel.

13. Pilot Attendance is the deployment of a Pilot for operations other than normal pilotage (berthing, unberthing and

shifting) of vessels. Eg. Salvage, mid-stream and offshore cargo/survey operations.

14. Berth Occupancy Charge is assessed on the Length-over-all (LOA) range in metres of the vessel. The LOA shall be as

specified in the Lloyd’s Register of Shipping. The berth occupancy charges commence when the first line is sent ashore
during berthing and ends when the last line is taken off the bollard when unberthing.

terms_source_pages.title: General Terms and Conditions — printed page 66
terms_source_pages.searchable_transcription:
15. Pilotage is compulsory in all Pilotage Districts. Pilotage shall be paid even if a Pilot is not deployed on the vessel. For
the avoidance of doubt, all Supply/Support vessels moving in and out of the Sekondi Naval base shall be required to
pay Pilotage to the Authority.

16. Pilotage, Towage, Mooring/Unmooring and Shifting charges shall be assessed on the Gross Tons (GT) range of the
vessel or craft as specified in the Lloyds Register of Shipping.

17. Pilotage, Towage and Mooring/Unmooring of a vessel not under steam (i.e. with stalled/dead engine) or in distress shall
attract double the relevant rates specified.

18. A vessel berthing successively at several berths during a port call, the berthing time from mooring at the first berth to
unmooring at the last berth shall be considered as one continuous berthing duration for the purpose for charging Berth
Occupancy.

19. A vessel or craft using the anchorage on the request of the Authority due to reasons such as temporary unavailability of
a berth, bad weather, etc. shall be exempted from the payment of Anchorage Charges.

20. A vessel or craft which intends to use the anchorage for reasons, other than on the request of the Authority, shall make
prior arrangements with the Harbour Master through his accredited agent by completing and submitting prescribed
forms — APPLICATION TO USE ANCHORAGE - ahead of the arrival of the vessel or within 12 hours of arrival.
Failure to complete the Application to Use Anchorage Forms shall attract a fine of US$5,000.00 in addition to the
charges accrued from the use of the anchorage. Vessels which do not have an accredited local agent shall be denied the
use of the anchorage.

21.The permission of the Authority shall be sought at all times before a private company providing under water services
is engaged to work in the Port. Failure to seek the written approval of the Authority shall attract a penalty of
US$10,000.00. The Authority shall reserve the right at any time to approve or disapprove such requests, and it may opt
to perform such a service if it considers it is capable of providing such a service. Where a private company provides the
service, it shall pay 25 per cent of the fees charged to the Authority as Royalty.

C. CARGO HANDLING CHARGES

1. Where the charges specified in these Tariffs are assessed on the weight of the cargo, the higher of the Cubic
Measurement (CBM) to deadweight Tonne shall apply at all times. A Tonne equals 1,000 kilograms or one cubic meter
(CBM).

2. Where minimum charge does not apply, charges will be calculated to the nearest Tonne. E.g. 5.2 Tonnes will be charged
as 5 tonnes and 5.5 tonnes will be charged as 6 tonnes.

3. Heavy lifts shall be charged using the Cubic Measurement (CBM) or deadweight, whichever yields the higher revenue.
However, in the case of conventional cargo, the heavy lift rates (i.e. the rates for lifts 6 to 10 tonnes and lifts above 10
tonnes) shall be applied if the deadweight of the cargo is used as the basis for charging.

4. For Oil and gas cargo, the heavy lift rates (i.e. the rates for lifts 6 to 10 tonnes, lifts above 10 and up to 20 Tonnes and
lifts above 20 tonnes) shall be applied if the deadweight of the cargo is used as the basis for charging.

5. Ifthe CBM is used as the basis for charging heavy lifts, in Notes C3 and C4 above; then the standard rate (i.e. the rate
for lifts up to 5 tonnes) shall be used as rate for charging.

6. The cargo handling rates prescribed in this tariff apply to handling during normal working hours. Where overtime is
worked additional charges shall be levied. For stevedoring operations and ship related shore operations, overtime shall
be assessed on the basis of the volume (tonnes, TEUs, Units) of cargo worked. With respect to storage related shore
operations, overtime shall be assessed on the basis of the number of persons deployed and the actual overtime hours
worked.

Where additional services are required to be performed, additional charges shall be levied to cover the reasonable cost
of the services provided.

Fertilizers, including those in containers, shipped for agricultural purposes shall be exempted from the dangerous cargo
rate and charged as the rate for non-hazardous (general) goods. This includes transit cargo.

Live animals shall be delivered/shipped per the direct route at all times. The receiver shall provide feed, water and
other needs of the livestock.

The cargo receiver/shipper shall supply at no cost to the Stevedore the grabs, hoppers and other dry bulk handling
equipment required for loading/discharging Dry Bulk and Semi-Bulk cargoes.

. All heavy-duty equipment (HDE) including equipment moving on metal tracks, earth moving equipment, mining dump

trucks, pay loaders, crawlers, road compactors and rollers, mobile cranes, compressors, asphalt laying machines,
mobile generators, etc. and others that do not normally ply on public roads shall be considered conventional cargo and
charged as such.

All auto mobiles that are intended to carry goods and/or personnel including cars, vans, buses, agricultural tractors,
building and civil engineering construction dump trucks, that do normally ply on public roads shall be considered as

Unpacked Vehicles and charged as such.

Vehicles/Trailers in stacks of more than one i.e. two, three, four etc., stuffed with other vehicles/trailers shall attract
rates as per the vehicle/trailer type for the number of vehicles/trailers in the stack.

Vehicles which are stuffed with personal effects or goods other than vehicle accessories shall attract one-half of the
applicable rates specified under the Schedules.

Similarly, trailers stuffed with goods e.g. knocked down vehicle parts and components, machinery and equipment,
tyres, etc. will attract one-half of the charge.

Vehicles stacked on trailers will attract the appropriate charge for the vehicle type.

Vehicles/Trailers stuffed with knocked down vehicle components, knocked down or full units of machinery and
equipment shall be considered as stuffed vehicles and charged as such.

Articulated vehicles shall be charged as two units — i.e. as a utility vehicle and a trailer unit.

Stevedorage, Craneage, Labour Charges and Terminal Handling Charges of Transhipment Unpacked Vehicles are for
both Inbound and Outbound and shall be charged against the Inbound vessel only.

Dangerous Goods Group I shall not be stored in the Port. These should be routed through direct mode at all times.

Transhipment of containers with Dangerous Goods shall be routed through the direct ship-to-ship mode at all times.
These should not be stored in the port.

It shall be the duty of the owner of a container RO-RO vessel carrying containers and project cargo to maintain
appropriate stock of cargo handling equipment on the ship for use by Licensed Stevedores. The use of such ship
equipment by Licensed Stevedores shall not attract any charges from the Ship.

Where a container RO-RO vessel carrying containers and project cargo does not have appropriate equipment on the
ship, the Stevedores shall charge the ship for the deployment of their equipment on the ship at the Craneage rate for all
containers moved across ramp.

Stevedores shall not be required to make any payments to the ship with regard to the use of ship equipment e.g. cranes
and derricks, cargo handling equipment (i.e. lift trucks, tractor-trailer sets, gears, etc.). This includes cargo handling

equipment maintained on roll on -roll off vessels.

terms_source_pages.title: General Terms and Conditions — printed page 68
terms_source_pages.searchable_transcription:
